items.q: Quis bracchium Quīntī scalpellō secuit?
items.en: Who cut Quintus' arm with a scalpel?
items.hint: the nominative subject; scalpellō suō acūtō is an ablative of instrument

items.q: Quandō medicus pedem Quīntī tetigit?
items.en: When did the doctor touch Quintus' foot?
answers: cum Quīntus herī dē altā arbore cecidisset
cum herī dē altā arbore cecidisset
choices: cum Quīntus herī dē altā arbore cecidisset
items.hint: a cum clause with the pluperfect subjunctive (cecidisset)

items.q: Quōmodo fīlius Aemiliae sānābitur, ut ipsa spērat?
items.en: How will Aemilia's son be healed, as she hopes?
answers: nōn operā medicī, sed diīs iuvantibus
items.hint: an ablative absolute with a present participle ('with the gods helping'); fore = futūrum esse

items.q: Quā condiciōne Sextus sē dēfendere scit?
items.en: On what condition does Sextus know how to defend himself?
answers: dummodo cum singulīs certet, sē dēfendere scit
items.hint: dummodo + present subjunctive ('provided that'); singulīs = one at a time

items.q: Utrīus reī studiōsior est Sextus: legendī an pugnandī?
items.en: Which is Sextus keener on: reading or fighting?
items.hint: gerunds in the genitive after studiōsus, compared with quam

items.q: Quibus rēbus Mārcus studet?
items.en: What is Marcus keen on?
items.hint: studēre takes the dative; nōn tam … quam = 'not so much … as'

items.q: Quid Aemilia ā Cornēliō quaerit?
items.en: What does Aemilia ask Cornelius?
items.hint: an indirect question with the present subjunctive (certent); rētibus is an ablative of means

items.q: Quandō gladiātor rētī implicitus nōn interficitur?
items.en: When is a gladiator caught in the net not killed?
answers: sī tam fortiter pugnāvit ut spectātōrēs eum vīvere velint
nisi tam fortiter pugnāvit ut spectātōrēs eum vīvere velint
choices: sī tam fortiter pugnāvit ut spectātōrēs eum vīvere velint
items.hint: a result clause: tam … ut + present subjunctive (velint), inside a nisi clause

items.q: Quid victor accipit?
items.en: What does the winner receive?
items.hint: the accusative object of accipit; dum + present indicative = 'while'

items.q: Cūr Cornēlius ex novissimīs circēnsibus maestus abiit?
items.en: Why did Cornelius leave the last races sad?
answers: cum ille aurīga cui plērīque favēbant ex currū lāpsus occīsus esset
quia aurīga ex currū lāpsus occīsus erat
quia aurīga cui plērīque spectātōrēs favēbant occīsus erat
items.hint: a cum clause with the pluperfect subjunctive passive (occīsus esset); favēre takes the dative (cui)

items.q: Quōs lūdōs Fabia praefert?
items.en: Which games does Fabia prefer?
items.hint: the accusative object of praeferō; mālō + infinitive follows

items.q: Cūr Iuppiter sē in formam Amphitryōnis mūtāvit?
items.en: Why did Jupiter change himself into the form of Amphitryon?
items.hint: a purpose clause: ut + imperfect subjunctive; cum putāret is a causal cum clause

items.q: Cūr fēminae in theātrum veniunt, ut Ovidius scrībit?
items.en: Why do women come to the theatre, as Ovid writes?
answers: spectātum veniunt, veniunt ut ipsae spectentur
items.hint: a supine of purpose (spectātum) and a purpose clause with the present subjunctive passive (ut … spectentur)

items.q: Quās virī in theātrō spectāre veniunt, ut Fabia dīcit?
items.en: Whom do men come to watch in the theatre, according to Fabia?
items.hint: the accusative object inside a purpose clause (ut … spectent)

items.q: Cūr poēta in circum vēnit?
items.en: Why did the poet come to the circus?
answers: ut cum puellā loquerētur et cum eā sedēret
ut loquerētur cum eā et cum eā sedēret
ut loquerer tēcum vēnī tēcumque sedērem
items.hint: purpose clauses: ut + imperfect subjunctive (loquerer, sedērem) in verse order

items.q: Quid puella in circō spectat?
items.en: What does the girl watch at the circus?
items.hint: the accusative plural of a fourth-declension noun; spectēmus is a hortatory subjunctive

items.q: Quot ōscula puella poētae dedit?
items.en: How many kisses did the girl give the poet?
items.hint: an indeclinable numeral with ōscula (accusative plural)

items.q: Ad quam Catullus carmina bella scrīpsit?
items.en: To whom did Catullus write his charming poems?
items.hint: ad + accusative; iuvant takes an accusative of the person (mē)

items.q: Quis mortuus est?
items.en: Who has died?
items.hint: the nominative subject of a deponent perfect (mortuus est); meae puellae is a genitive

items.q: Quō passer nunc it?
items.en: Where is the sparrow going now?
items.hint: illūc … unde ('to that place from which'); negant introduces an indirect statement

items.q: Cūr ocellī puellae rubent?
items.en: Why are the girl's little eyes red?
items.hint: a gerund in the ablative giving the cause ('from weeping')

items.q: Quid nōbīs dormiendum est, cum semel occidit brevis lūx?
items.en: What must we sleep, once the brief light has set?
items.hint: a gerundive with est (dormienda) and a dative of agent (nōbīs = by us)

items.q: Quot bāsia poēta post mīlle petit?
items.en: How many kisses does the poet ask for after the thousand?
items.hint: an indeclinable numeral after dā (imperative); mī = mihi

items.q: Cūr Catullus et Lesbia bāsia conturbābunt?
items.en: Why will Catullus and Lesbia muddle up the count of kisses?
items.hint: a negative purpose clause: nē + present subjunctive

items.q: Ubi scrībere oportet quod mulier amantī dīcit?
items.en: Where should one write what a woman says to her lover?
answers: in ventō et in rapidā aquā
items.hint: in + ablative; oportet takes an infinitive as its subject

items.q: Quālem esse Lesbiam Catullus postrēmō intellēxit?
items.en: What did Catullus finally realise Lesbia was like?
answers: īnfīdam et amōre suō indignam esse
items.hint: an indirect statement with accusative adjectives; indignus takes the ablative (amōre)

items.q: Dēsiitne Catullus Lesbiam amāre?
items.en: Did Catullus stop loving Lesbia?
items.hint: a yes/no question with -ne; neque tamen = 'and yet … not'

items.q: Quid Paula Iūlium recitāre vult?
items.en: What does Paula want Julius to recite?
items.hint: quīn + indicative ('why not …?'); the object is in the accusative plural

items.q: Quandō Fabullus bene apud Catullum cēnābit?
items.en: When will Fabullus dine well at Catullus' house?
answers: sī sēcum attulerit bonam atque magnam cēnam
sī tēcum attuleris bonam atque magnam cēnam
sī bonam atque magnam cēnam attulerit
items.hint: sī + future perfect (attuleris) with a future main verb

items.q: Ubi Cornēlius librōs Mārtiālis semper sēcum fert?
items.en: Where does Cornelius always carry Martial's books with him?
items.hint: in + ablative (in sinū = in the fold of his toga)

items.q: Cūr Mārtiālis libellōs suōs Pontiliānō nōn mittit?
items.en: Why doesn't Martial send Pontilianus his little books?
items.hint: a negative purpose clause: nē + present subjunctive

items.q: Quis versiculōs in Mārtiālem scrībere nārrātur?
items.en: Who is said to write little verses against Martial?
items.hint: a nominative subject with a passive verb of saying + infinitive (nārrātur scrībere)

items.q: Quā condiciōne Māmercus esse potest quidquid vult?
items.en: On what condition can Mamercus be whatever he wants?
answers: dummodo nīl recitet, estō quidquid vult
items.hint: dummodo + present subjunctive ('provided that'); estō is a future imperative

items.q: Quae niveōs dentēs habet?
items.en: Which woman has snow-white teeth?
items.hint: the nominative subject in the second half of the line (the word order is crossed)

items.q: Quandō Gellia patrem āmissum nōn flet?
items.en: When does Gellia not weep for her lost father?
items.hint: cum + present indicative (a repeated occasion); āmissum is a perfect passive participle

items.q: Quot ferē epigrammata Cornēlius recitāvit?
items.en: About how many epigrams did Cornelius recite?
items.hint: a numeral inside an ablative absolute (epigrammatīs recitātīs); fīnem facit + genitive gerund
